newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CAR SALES SOAR NEARLY 40 PCT IN 10 MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CAR SALES SOAR NEARLY 40 PCT IN 10 MONTHS.

text.p: New car sales in Poland jumped nearly 40 percent in the first ten months of 1996 compared with the same period last year, showing the biggest growth rate in Europe, an independent monitoring agency reported on Monday.

A monthly survey by the private Samar agency, which monitors the domestic car market, showed 321,005 new passenger cars were registered in January-October, compared with 229,685 in the same period last year.
During the 10 months, the number of newly registered delivery vehicles jumped by nearly 63 percent to 39,687 units, compared with the same period last year.
Samar, quoting figures by the Association des Constructeurs Europeens d'Automoblies, said Poland had the fastest new car sales growth rate in Europe.
It said Poland was followed by Norway and Ireland, where cars registration growth reached 35 percent and 31 percent over the period with 107,600 and 110,800 cars sold respectively.
Germany, the first in new car sales volume, registered estimated 3,001,800 passenger cars in the January-October period, 6.5 percent more than last year.
In Poland, the domestic unit of Fiat Spa led the market with 134,530 cars and a 42 percent market share.
Other top sellers include Daewoo-FSO, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Corp , General Motors' German unit Adam Opel AG and Renault .
Samar Director Wojciech Drzewiecki earlier said the robust cars sales was fuelled by growth in real wages and more attractive terms of bank financing of car purchases.
